Pinterest Marketing for Coaches and Course Creators

By Marie Glow StudioUpdated September 23, 2026

Nobody searches Pinterest for the name of your program. They search for the thing that is bothering them: a messy schedule, a stalled business, a habit they cannot keep. Pinterest marketing for coaches works when each pin answers one of those searches and then leads to a page that keeps the relationship going, usually an email opt-in. Your name and your course title come second.

Start from the problem, not the offer

A pin that says "Join my 8 week program" asks a stranger to commit before they know you. A pin that says "How to plan a week when you feel behind on everything" answers a search first and introduces you second. The same expertise, framed as the question your ideal client already has, is what gets found. Our post on Pinterest marketing for digital products explains the teach first approach that also applies to courses.

Four things worth pinning

1. Your lead magnet

A checklist, workbook or short guide that solves one small problem is the easiest pin to justify, because the click is low commitment. Name the result in the pin title, and send it to a focused opt-in page, not your homepage.

2. Blog posts

Each post that answers a complete question can carry several pins, each aimed at a different search angle. See Pinterest strategy for bloggers for grouping posts by keyword.

3. Course or program pages

Pin these, but as the minority. A pin about the problem the course solves usually earns a more receptive click than one that only names the course.

4. Email opt-ins

Newsletter signup pages can be pinned when the pin promises something specific to receive, not just "subscribe."

Find the phrases your clients actually type

You do not need a paid tool to begin. Try this:

  1. Type a core topic from your work into Pinterest search, such as "morning routine" or "time management."
  2. Note the suggestions that appear as you type, since they reflect real searches.
  3. Write down the more specific versions, for example a topic plus a life stage or a situation.
  4. Choose one phrase per pin and put it near the start of the title.

Longer, more specific phrases are easier to match and closer to the moment someone needs help. How to find long tail keywords on Pinterest goes deeper, and the sections on keyword research cover where to place them.

The link between Pinterest and email

A visitor from Pinterest rarely buys a coaching package on the first visit. What you can do is invite them to stay in touch. Send pins to a page with one clear next step, an email opt-in, and follow up with a short welcome sequence. This is what turns saves and clicks into a list you own. Pinterest and email marketing explains how the two support each other.

Match the pin to where the reader is

People at different stages search differently. Someone early in the problem searches broadly and wants an explanation. Someone further along searches for a method, a template or a way to get support. Plan a few pins for each stage: a broad idea pin that leads to a blog post, a how to pin that leads to a lead magnet, and a smaller number of pins that lead to a program. That spread keeps your feed useful, and it gives the visitor a natural path from learning to trusting to buying, without pushing anyone before they are ready. Keep your promises small and specific, and never state results you cannot back up.

A simple pin to inbox check

  • Does the pin title contain the phrase someone would search?
  • Does the description say what the visitor will get after clicking?
  • Does the destination deliver exactly what the pin promised?
  • Is there one obvious next step on that page?

If your destination page is the weak point, a one page website for coaches and course creators gives you a clean place to send people. Selling downloads or templates as well? See a Shopify website for digital product sellers.

Frequently asked questions

What should a coach pin on Pinterest?

Pin content that answers a problem people search for: lead magnets, blog posts, course pages and email opt-ins. Lead with the problem in the pin title, and make promotional course pins the smaller share.

Should coaches send Pinterest traffic to a course page or an email opt-in?

For most visitors, an email opt-in is the better first step, because a stranger rarely buys a program on a first visit. A lead magnet or opt-in page lets you follow up and invite them to the course later.

How do I find keywords for coaching pins without a paid tool?

Type a core topic into Pinterest search and note the suggestions that appear. Those phrases reflect real searches, and the more specific versions are easier to match and closer to what a client needs.

How long before Pinterest brings coaching leads?

Expect weeks or months of consistent publishing. Pins can keep surfacing over time, so it works best as a long term channel that feeds your email list rather than a quick launch tool.
